notes:
Account: enterprise fintech trading platform. Negotiating Reserved GPU pools for low-latency personalization + high-throughput reranking. Primary stakeholders: CTO (Maya Chen), Head of ML (Luis Ortega), infra lead (Samir Patel). AE: Jordan Reyes; SE: Priya Kulkarni engaged for sizing + perf tests.

Summary of recent calls: 
- 2026-02-20 kickoff (Fireflies ff_20260220_call_8471): scoped workloads, initial perf targets. Quote: "sub-200ms p95 is deal-breaker for live personalization".
- 2026-03-01 POC kickoff (ff_20260301_poc_kickoff_9023): deployed staging dedicated pool; smoke tests run.

Technical requirements (top-level):
- Workload mix: 60% real-time personalization (short contexts ~32-64 tokens), 30% reranking (multi-pass scoring across candidate lists), 10% nightly batch embeddings for analytics.
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 200ms for 64-token personalization requests (95% of traffic), p99 <= 400ms for heavier rerank flows (multi-candidate scoring).
- Throughput guarantees: baseline sustained throughput target ~1,200 inference QPS across pool with 2x burst capability to 2,500 QPS for market open spikes.
- Reserved capacity ask: initial committed pool equivalent to 16 x A100-80GB (or vendor equivalent), staged to 32 in Q3, 48 by end of year depending on adoption.
- Multi-region plan: primary in us-west2, DR/secondary in us-east1. Each region: 2 AZs active with autoscaling limited to reserved pool. Warm-standby in secondary region sized at 15% of primary committed capacity for cross-region failover; additional cold-headroom target 20% overall.
- Failover expectations: cross-region failover under partial outage should preserve critical routing for personalization traffic (route to warm standby). Cold start policy acceptable for non-critical batch jobs.
- Fallback model policy: during capacity pressure, prefer automatic route to quantized model variant (saves tokens/cost) with fall-through to hosted fallback if both dedicated and private are saturated.

Security/compliance notes:
- Must support corporate SSO (SAML) + KMS integration for model keys. Data residency: EU customer data must remain in eu-west1 or equivalent; working through redlines. SOC2 and ISO27001 required for contract. Audit logging retention 7 years for some trading flows (negotiable).

POC results to date:
- Baseline perf tests on staging dedicated pool: p95 ~185ms for 64-token personalization on single-A100 equiv (with continuous batching tuned). P99 spikes seen during synthetic candidate-heavy rerank tests ~420ms. Need kernel selection/kv-cache tuning for reranking pass.
- Observed 18% headroom on current staging config; SE recommends reserving extra 20% per-region to meet failover SLA.

Commercial / SLA negotiation highlights:
- Crimson Lattice wants SLA with latency SLO credits (not just uptime). Asking for: 99.95% uptime + latency SLOs measured at account edge (p95/p99) with service credits sliding scale. Legal pushing back on liability cap — currently at standard Redwood template; CL asking for higher cap given fintech risk.
- Procurement timeline: internal budget sign-off targeted by 2026-04, contract signature target 2026-05. Forecast ARR in range $750k-$1.5M depending on committed capacity.

Open actions / next steps:
- Jordan / Priya to deliver final capacity spec doc by 2026-03-12 (includes SKU mapping, AZ placement, warm-standby sizing). (Assigned: Priya)
- SE to run rerank kernel tuning pass and deliver improved p99 report by 2026-03-15.
- Legal to review SLA redlines; meeting with Crimson legal 2026-03-18.
- Clarify EU data residency path & confirm whether private (on-prem) package required for specific trading desks.

Snippets from interviews: "We need predictable latency during market open spikes — capacity planning must be conservative, willing to pay premium for reserved headroom."

Misc references: pricing deck and security FAQ in Drive. Jira escalation RDW-12893 tracking kernel tuning issues.
